title: Granola potato (patatas Granola): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Granola potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Granola potato is a potato variety. About 100 days to harvest, 24 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Granola is a registered potato variety, also sold or known as patatas Granola. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1983. It comes from registered by BSU NPRCRTC (introduced variety). It takes about 100 days from planting to harvest, with 24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for patatas Granola, this is the same potato. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [potato variety finder](/crop-varieties/potato), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 100 days from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Granola potato takes about 100 days from planting to harvest. That is 3.5 days faster than the average of the 11 potato varieties with a day count, 103.5 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 24 t/ha beats the average of its group, 21.79. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 100 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit potato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [late blight](/diseases/late-blight), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 24 t/ha in registry trials, 19.4 t/ha as the table check in BSU trials.
**Fruit:** Firm flesh, slight to average color change on cooking.
Registered in 1983 with the Philippine Seed Board.
More late blight than resistant BSU clones in trials.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of the three potatoes Benguet and Mountain Province farmers prefer most, and the seed potato URC's farmer program distributes. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Granola potato

It suits highland areas. Potato grows in the cool highlands of Benguet, Mountain Province and Bukidnon. Plant clean seed tubers, and pick a variety rated against late blight for the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is patatas Granola the same as Granola?
items.a: Yes. patatas Granola is another name for Granola. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 100 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Granola?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
